:::{#sol-cross-entropy-expectation}

1. The variable $Y$ equals $-\log_2 \tfrac{1}{4} = 2$ when $X \in \set{1, 3}$,
   and $-\log_2 \tfrac{1}{2} = 1$ when $X = 2$.
   So $\P(Y = 2) = p_1 + p_3 = \tfrac{3}{4}$ and $\P(Y = 1) = p_2 = \tfrac{1}{4}$, and

   $$
   \ba
   \E{Y}
   &= 2 \cd \tfrac{3}{4} + 1 \cd \tfrac{1}{4} \\
   &= \tfrac{7}{4}.
   \ea
   $$

2. From the definition,

   $$
   \ba
   H(p, q)
   &= -\tfrac{1}{2} \log_2 \tfrac{1}{4} - \tfrac{1}{4} \log_2 \tfrac{1}{2} - \tfrac{1}{4} \log_2 \tfrac{1}{4} \\
   &= \tfrac{1}{2} \cd 2 + \tfrac{1}{4} \cd 1 + \tfrac{1}{4} \cd 2 \\
   &= \tfrac{7}{4}.
   \ea
   $$

   This equals $\E{Y}$.
   The two calculations group the same three terms differently:
   part 1 first combines outcomes 1 and 3, which have the same value of $Y$.

3. Let $g(k) = -\log q_k$.
   This is finite for every $k$ with $p_k > 0$, which are the values $X$ takes with positive probability.
   By [LOTUS](expectation.qmd#thm-lotus),

   $$
   \ba
   \E{-\log q_X}
   &= \E{g(X)} \\
   &= \sum_{k : p_k > 0} g(k) \cd \P(X = k) \\
   &= -\sum_{k : p_k > 0} p_k \log q_k \\
   &= -\sumto{k}{K} p_k \log q_k \\
   &= H(p, q).
   \ea
   $$

   The fourth line adds the terms with $p_k = 0$, which are $0$ by the convention in the definition.

4. If $q_k = 0$ and $p_k > 0$, then $H(p, q) = \infty$ by the definition.
   Also $-\log q_X = \infty$ with probability $p_k > 0$, and $-\log q_X \ge 0$ always,
   so $\E{-\log q_X} = \infty$ as well.
   Both sides are infinite, so they are still equal.

:::
